title: Ask Clang why the loop stayed scalar

cast.name: Nia
cast.role: Junior compiler engineer, eager to blame the optimization level

cast.name: Len
cast.role: Staff engineer who asks for the compiler's evidence

glossary.note: One operation handles several independent values.

key_points: Ask the vectorizer for missed and analysis remarks at the exact loop.
A loop-carried dependency may make adjacent iterations unsafe to combine.
A transformation is not a speedup; inspect target code and benchmark representative inputs.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: At review, Nia blames Clang for leaving a prefix sum scalar.

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: I built at O three. Why no vector instructions? Each loop seems small.

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Each iteration reads the previous result. Can independent lanes preserve that dependency?

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: Let us ask the vectorizer instead of guessing?

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Clang prints success, missed, and analysis remarks. They separate safety blockers from cost-model choices.

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: In this illustrative prefix sum, imagine a remark points to the loop-carried dependency. Check the source line before editing.

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: A separate copy loop differs: pointers may overlap. The compiler may need runtime checks before a single-instruction, multiple-data operation.

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Use restrict only when callers guarantee no overlap. A false promise can change program behavior.

visuals.title: contract is a promise
code: /* use restrict only if ranges cannot overlap */

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: If it vectorizes, is it faster?

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Inspect target instructions, including remainder and runtime-check paths. Then benchmark realistic lengths and alignment; short loops or memory bandwidth can erase the gain.

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: The answer is not “turn optimization up.” Read the remark, fix the blocker if possible, inspect machine code, and measure.

visuals.title: debugging order
code: remark → source dependency → target code → benchmark

expect.note: The explanatory note states why this illustrative loop remains scalar.
